subject: general
question: Which of the following best encapsulates the concept of a 'stored-program computer'as introduced by the Von Neumann architecture?

options.text: A computer that can only execute a fixed set of instructions hardwired into its circuitry
A computer that relies primarily on external storage devices for program execution
A computer where both data and instructions are stored in the same primary memory for sequential execution
A computer that utilises separate memory units for data and instructions to optimise processing speed

solution:
The Correct answer is __**A computer where both data and instructions are stored in the same primary memory for sequential execution**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Von Neumann architecture** introduced the concept of a stored-program computer.
 
• In this architecture, both **data and instructions** are stored together in the same memory unit, enabling the processor to access them sequentially.
 
• This design uses a single memory space for storing both **programs (instructions)** and **data**, eliminating the need for separate storage units.
 
• The stored-program concept allows flexibility, enabling computers to execute different programs without hardware modifications.
 
• The architecture consists of key components such as a **Central Processing Unit (CPU)**, **memory**, and **I/O devices**.
 
• The CPU executes instructions sequentially, fetching them from memory, decoding them, and performing operations as specified.
 
• This model laid the foundation for modern computing systems and is used in almost all general-purpose computers today.
 
• The concept revolutionized computing by introducing programmability and reducing dependency on external hardware for processing instructions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **A computer that can only execute a fixed set of instructions hardwired into its circuitry**__

 __
 
• This describes an **early computing model**, such as those used in the pre-Von Neumann era.
 
• These systems, often referred to as **hardwired computers**, lacked flexibility and required physical rewiring to change instructions.
 
 
 
• **A computer that relies primarily on external storage devices for program execution**__
 __
 
• This describes systems that depend heavily on **external media** such as tapes or disks for program storage and execution.
 
• Such systems are less efficient compared to the stored-program model introduced by Von Neumann.
 
 
 
• **A computer that utilises separate memory units for data and instructions to optimise processing speed**__
 
 
• This describes the **Harvard architecture**, which is distinct from the Von Neumann model.
 
• In the Harvard architecture, separate memory units for data and instructions enable parallel access, improving processing speed.
